audit.whatIsWrong: The grounding interaction is real but attributed to the wrong ability throughout. early says Miasma "cancels your Devour approach"; whys[1] says it "grounds your Devour approach"; wants.foe[0] says "your Devour approach is blocked and your dashes are cancelled".
audit.why: Grounded disables MOVEMENT abilities. Devour is a 250-range point-and-click cast and is not affected by grounding at all — you can still eat her while standing in Miasma. What the pool actually switches off is Abyssal Dive, which is a blink and is Tahm Kench's only mobility. Tahm Kench also has no "dashes" plural. As written the reader will believe their ultimate is disabled (it is not) and will not realise their blink is (it is).
audit.corrected: Miasma grounds you, which disables Abyssal Dive specifically. Devour still works inside the pool.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json (W: "Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities")
League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Abyssal Dive is a blink and is listed as disabled by Grounded; Devour cast range 250

audit.whatIsWrong: Miasma is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in nine separate strings across both layers, and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Miasma is 24s at rank 1 — one of the longest non-ultimate cooldowns you will play against in the top lane. That is the entire punish window and the reader cannot see it. Once she has spent the pool you have roughly twenty seconds where your blink works and she has no way to cut your angle.
audit.corrected: 24s at rank 1, falling to 16s at rank 5, added wherever the length band allowed.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal recommendation anywhere, despite the entire late-game plan being an attrition war against Twin Fang.
audit.why: Twin Fang "heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt" and is on a 0.75s cooldown, so in an extended fight she is healing continuously off the same chip damage the entry tells you to absorb. spikes[3] promises your grey-health healing "outraces her sustained Twin Fang DPS" without noting that she is healing too. Grievous Wounds is what actually makes that race winnable.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into the first-item spike.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json (E: Twin Fang, cd 0.75, "heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt")

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Tongue Lash's slow as reliable pressure and never mentions that Cassiopeia is unusually good at undoing it.
audit.why: Two kit pieces compound: Noxious Blast grants her Move Speed whenever it hits a champion, and Serpentine Grace makes ALL Move Speed bonuses more effective on her. So the poke she throws at you is also her answer to the slow you just applied, amplified. That is why the slow-and-walk-forward pattern that works elsewhere does not work here.
audit.corrected: Named in mid and in wants.foe[1] as the reason your slow does not stick.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json (P: "All Move Speed bonuses are more effective on Cassiopeia"; Q: "granting her increased Move Speed if she hits an enemy champion")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], wants.you[0] and late run the "stun and Devour" / "3 stacks ready to stun-Devour her" pattern.
audit.why: The Q stun at 3 stacks consumes all three stacks and Devour requires 3 stacks. Only one of the two can happen per stack cycle.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the eat.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: late and whys[6] describe "Abyssal Voyage repositioning" turning teamfights into a nightmare for her backline.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the removed pre-rework ultimate. The ability that actually reaches her backline is Abyssal Dive — a blink with a knockup attached, and its range grows to 1200 at rank 5, which is a genuinely relevant number against a stationary artillery mage.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive, with the 1200 rank-5 range and the knockup, which is a stronger and truer version of the same point.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff is "HARD" at 8.5/10 difficulty, but the packet win rate is 54.75% over 358 games — the second-best win rate in my slice.
audit.why: A 54.75% matchup is not a hard lane. The content-layer chart agrees with the win rate, giving Tahm Kench four stages and Cassiopeia only level 6, so the full layer is the outlier. Note also that the difficulty labels across this file do not track win rate generally: Pantheon at 56.58% is TRICKY while Swain at 57.06% is EVEN.
audit.corrected: No edit proposed. "HARD" (4 chars) cannot become "TRICKY" (6) or "EVEN" (4, but wrong direction) within the +/-10% band, and 8.5/10 -> 6/10 is likewise out of band. Flagged in notes.

edits.before: Tongue Lash has the range to contest her Noxious Blast poke — every CS trade you step up and hit her with Q stacks An Acquired Taste for free, and her poison ticks convert straight into Thick Skin grey health you will heal back between waves. Do not walk into her W Miasma pool under any circumstance: it grounds you, cancels your Devour approach, and lets her Twin Fang stack freely while you stand still. The gameplan is simple: Q her for stacks, hold Devour as the threat that keeps her from all-inning you, and heal through the poison in the wave-downtime between trades.
edits.after: Tongue Lash's 900 matches her Noxious Blast poke — every CS trade you step up and hit her with Q stacks An Acquired Taste for free, and her poison ticks convert straight into Thick Skin grey health you will heal back between waves. The gameplan is simple: Q her for stacks, hold Devour as the threat that stops her all-inning you, and heal through the poison between trades.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the honest lull — she extends her range advantage and can freely drop Miasma pools to cut off your angle every time you try to step up for stacks. Play for CS and stack fishing from maximum Tongue Lash range; do not force a Devour if her W pool is between you. Level 6 is hers: Petrifying Gaze is an instant face-stun on anyone walking toward her, and she will hold it specifically to answer your 3-stack combo window. Respect the facing, farm through it, and wait for a wave state where she has to step up to you rather than kite back.

It is 24s at rank 1 though, so the moment it is spent you have a long window where Abyssal Dive works again. Play for CS from maximum Tongue Lash range, and know your slow decays fast on her: Noxious Blast speeds her up and Serpentine Grace amplifies every move-speed bonus she gets. Level 6 is hers: Petrifying Gaze stuns anyone facing her, and she holds it for your commit.

notes:
The grounding interaction was the interesting one here. It was present in the entry but pinned to the wrong ability in three separate places — Miasma was described as blocking "your Devour approach" and cancelling "your dashes". Grounded disables movement abilities, so what it actually switches off is Abyssal Dive, Tahm Kench's only mobility. Devour is a 250-range point-and-click and works perfectly well from inside the pool. As written the entry talked a player out of the one thing that still works and failed to warn them about the thing that stops working.

The full layer for this matchup refers to Cassiopeia as "he"/"him" in tldr, winCon and tradeGood. I corrected the pronouns in the strings I was already editing.

DIFFICULTY MISMATCH: full.diff is "HARD" at 8.5/10 against a 54.75% win rate over 358 games — the second-highest win rate in my slice. The content-layer chart agrees with the win rate (Tahm Kench takes four of seven stages); the full layer is the outlier. I could not fix it inside the length band. More broadly the diff labels in this file do not track win rate at all: Pantheon at 56.58% is TRICKY, Swain at 57.06% is EVEN, Teemo at 54.57% is HARD. Whatever generated those labels was not reading the win-rate table.

Smallest sample in my slice at 358 games — worth knowing before weighting this entry heavily.
